title: What-if token burst & safety stock analysis — hosted API peak headroom (2026Q3)
content:
Purpose:
This working note explores several realistic "what-if" surge scenarios for the Hosted API and derives recommended headroom and safety-stock targets (tokens/sec and QPS) by region. The goal is to produce actionable GPU-slice and routing knobs the infra team can implement before Q3 2026 traffic season.

Summary (one-line):
Recommend region-level safety-stock equivalent to 20% of steady-state GPU capacity plus a global surge buffer equal to 1.8x baseline for normal peaks and 2.6x for extreme bursts; enable fast fallback routing to quantized variants and pre-warmed spare slices to meet 99.995% availability during bursts.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline observed peak (last 90 days, 95th percentile): 1,200,000 tokens/sec global across hosted API.
- Average tokens per request: 40 tokens (weighted mix chat + completion).
- Model mix by token-weight: 60% medium family (dedicated runtime profile A), 30% large family (profile B), 10% experimental/fallback.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (mixed-weighted average, accounting for batching and KV cache): 30,000 tokens/sec per A100-like slice for mixed-profile workload.
- Goal SLOs: 99.99% availability, p95 latency < 250ms on typical routes.

Derived baseline metrics: (rounded)
- Baseline QPS = tokens/sec / tokens_per_req = 1,200,000 / 40 = 30,000 QPS.
- Baseline GPU count needed = baseline_tokens / tokens_per_gpu = 1,200,000 / 30,000 = 40 GPUs (equivalent full slices).

Why headroom > 1.0x is required:
- Bursty traffic patterns (product launches, viral events) cause short-term amplification (fan-out, retries) that increase token cost by 2–3x for short windows.
- Model degradation/failures require quick fallback to compatible quantized variants; fallbacks increase per-token GPU cost by ~1.2x–1.5x.
- Regional network flare-ups (CDN re-routing) can concentrate traffic into a single region.

Scenario definitions and recommended targets:
1) Normal peak (expected seasonal spikes)
- Multiplier: 1.5x baseline tokens/sec -> 1,800,000 tokens/sec.
- Equivalent QPS (~40 t/request): 45,000 QPS.
- GPU required (1.5x): 60 GPUs.
- Recommendation: maintain 1.5x auto-scale headroom across regions by policy + 10% pre-warmed spare slices to reduce cold-start latency.

2) High burst (marketing/event driven, ~1 in 20 days)
- Multiplier: 2.6x baseline -> 3,120,000 tokens/sec.
- QPS: 78,000 QPS.
- GPU required: 104 GPUs.
- Recommendation: safety-stock = "regional reserve" equal to 20% of regional steady-state fleet + fast-burst global pool (20 GPUs) that can be throttled across regions via smart routing.

3) Extreme multi-region failover (1 in 250)
- Characteristics: traffic from EU/Asia re-routed into US because of networking outage; local autoscale delayed by 2–5 minutes.
- Multiplier effective in one region: 3.5x local baseline -> regional tokens/sec spike equivalent to absorbing additional 40% of global peak.
- Recommendation: ensure each region can absorb +40% of global 95th percentile by reserving convertible capacity (GPU slices that can be force-migrated or re-sliced within 90s).

Regional breakdown (recommended steady-state slices and safety-stock)
- us-west-2: steady-state 16 GPUs, safety-stock 4 GPUs (25%) -> target reserve pool 20 GPUs.
- us-east-1: steady-state 12 GPUs, safety-stock 3 GPUs (25%) -> target 15 GPUs.
- eu-west-1: steady-state 8 GPUs, safety-stock 2 GPUs (25%) -> target 10 GPUs.
- ap-southeast-1: steady-state 4 GPUs, safety-stock 1 GPU (25%) -> target 5 GPUs.
Note: regional safety-stock percentages intentionally conservative (20–25%) to allow short-term absorption; global headroom is handled by central surge pool.

Operational controls recommended:
- Pre-warm policy: keep 10–15% of reserved slices in pre-warmed state for <100ms attach time.
- Fast-fallback routing: automatically route to quantized-compatible model family after 3 consecutive retries or >500ms queue time.
- Circuit breakers: per-customer and per-route token throttles that trigger queuing and token-based denial when region saturation > 85%.
- Progressive rollouts: during suspected demand spikes (marketing comms), cap non-critical routes to 50% to preserve headroom for core customers.

Cost and trade-offs (back-of-envelope):
- Additional 24 GPUs (difference between baseline 40 and extreme 104) as reserved/elastic capacity costs X/month — see attached spreadsheet (linked).
- If we prefer heavier reliance on quantized fallbacks, we can reduce physical GPUs by ~15% at the cost of ~10–20ms increased p95 latency and a small drop in output quality.

Quick checks/validation steps before adoption:
- Run synthetic burst simulations in staging (use traffic replay derived from 2025-11 spike B). Verify queue growth and failover latencies.
- Validate autoscaler cold-start attach times across regions (target < 90s for slice activation).
- Re-run cost model with updated token-per-GPU measurements from model family B (PR 218 measures currently in progress).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How do recent kernel optimizations in runtime v2.4 shift effective tokens/sec per GPU for the large family? (affects GPU counts).
- Canary policy for switching to quantized fallback under degraded performance — should this be per-route or global?
- Should dedicated enterprise tenants have isolated reserve pools or borrow from the global surge buffer?

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Evan R: run staging replay for Scenario 2 by 2026-02-20 (JIRA-RED-4128).
- Lina G: produce updated tokens-per-GPU measurement matrix for all model variants (deadline 2026-02-17).
- Chris P: prototype pre-warm slice attach API and measure <90s attach (deadline 2026-03-01).
- Maya P: draft runbook for region failover and circuit breaker thresholds (draft due 2026-02-24).

Appendix: quick calculation examples
- tokens/sec -> QPS: 3,120,000 tokens/sec / 40 = 78,000 QPS.
- GPU headroom multiplier: desired multiplier / tokens_per_gpu = GPUs_needed.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally uses conservative safety-stock to prioritize availability during viral events. If leadership prefers a cost-first posture we can produce an alternate plan with lower reserves and stronger quality fallbacks.
- Please add links to any relevant marketing calendars or expected product launches into JIRA-RED-4128 so we can mark protected intervals.
